claims.claim_text: The sensing element is a capacitive structure in a CMOS process whose capacitance changes by amounts measured in zeptofarads, and that change is converted to a voltage. Because the signal starts that small, Gaussian noise in the electronics sets a floor on how accurately mechanical motion can be resolved.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's working with zeptofarads
claims.speaker: Hank Zumbahlen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Hank Zumbahlen - Zoppa Zumbahlen Zateticism

claims.claim_text: The unfamiliar part for most engineers is the conversion itself: voltages and amplifiers are well understood, whereas turning gravity and tilt into an electrical number is not, and the understanding comes from having done it.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you start talking about measuring gravity and tilt and those types of things and converting that into an electrical number, that's kind of confusing
claims.speaker: Hank Zumbahlen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Hank Zumbahlen - Zoppa Zumbahlen Zateticism

claims.claim_text: The reading is dominated by gravity: acceleration measured by a stationary device is almost entirely the pull downward, which is why the simplest demonstration of the sensor is one that shows which way is down.
claims.quote_verbatim: acceleration is almost always gravity
claims.speaker: Elecia White
claims.episode_title: Is This A Show?

claims.claim_text: A gyroscope answers a different question and shows nothing while the device is still, because it responds to motion and gesture rather than to orientation.
claims.quote_verbatim: gyros are boring unless you're moving
claims.speaker: Elecia White
claims.episode_title: Is This A Show?

claims.claim_text: The technology was a genuine discontinuity rather than an incremental improvement: before micro-electromechanical parts existed there was no practical way to make these measurements at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: before that existed, there was really no way to do that kind of stuff
claims.speaker: Hank Zumbahlen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Hank Zumbahlen - Zoppa Zumbahlen Zateticism

claims.claim_text: What that replaced was bulky: an accelerometer meant an electromechanical assembly and a compass meant coils, with the mathematics left to the designer and no libraries to draw on.
claims.quote_verbatim: you put a gyroscope and, you know, electromechanical solution
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Warming Up To IoT - Tendentious Thermal Tools

claims.claim_text: Where those parts were unavailable, designers substituted a different physical principle entirely: a flight controller built from infrared thermopiles on each wingtip and the nose inferred bank and pitch from the sky being a different temperature to the ground, which still worked at night with the temperature relationship reversed.
claims.quote_verbatim: the sky is a different temperature to the ground
claims.speaker: Bruce Simson
claims.episode_title: Missle Man with Bruce Simson

claims.claim_text: A sensor can also be improvised from an unrelated part: replacing condenser microphones that suffered crosstalk and feedback, an electret microphone potted in epoxy inside a machined housing screwed directly to the instrument became, in effect, a purpose-built accelerometer.
claims.quote_verbatim: I made an accelerometer out of an electric microphone
claims.speaker: Julia Truchsess
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Julia Truchsess

claims.claim_text: Recovering position from acceleration requires integrating twice, and any jitter in the acceleration signal is magnified enormously by that double integration, which is why dead reckoning from an accelerometer alone does not work.
claims.quote_verbatim: accelerometers, you need to basically integrate them twice
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Absorptive Augmented Actuality

claims.claim_text: The direction of the calculation matters: differentiation is a mathematically noisy operation and integration is not, which is why integrating an accelerometer toward velocity and position behaves better than differentiating a position measurement would.
claims.quote_verbatim: differentiation is a mathematically noisy process versus integration, which isn't
claims.speaker: Gerry Roston
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Gerry Roston

claims.claim_text: It is still not good enough to navigate with: an attempt to track how far a boat had drifted by integrating acceleration ended with the position unknown.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm going to use an accelerometer to know how far my boat drifted
claims.speaker: Gerry Roston
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Gerry Roston

claims.claim_text: The same limit bounds fine position tracking on a person: the double integration can be made to work only if the subject stays completely still, so anything mounted on a moving head defeats it.
claims.quote_verbatim: the subject would have to be standing completely still
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: My Toothbrush Is Broadcasting

claims.claim_text: Consumer activity metrics are inferences rather than measurements: an interrupt indicates movement, the change between successive readings is interpreted as a step, and filtering does the rest — accurate enough to be useful and not the direct measurement it appears to be.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's all, you know, there's algorithms and there's all this stuff, but they're not, they're not super accurate
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Garbage Ninjas

claims.claim_text: Combining a three-axis accelerometer and a three-axis gyroscope into one digital part replaced two separate breakout boards, and the feature that mattered was the processor inside it fusing the raw readings into orientation on the chip.
claims.quote_verbatim: combined six axis accelerometer and gyroscope
claims.speaker: Jeff Roberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: On-chip fusion matters most where the host is small: doing the orientation mathematics in the sensor saves processing time and power on a low-power microcontroller that should be asleep as much as possible.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's a big deal because it saves you a lot of time, processing time and power
claims.speaker: Jeff Roberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: The vendor documented access to the raw accelerometer and gyroscope readings but published nothing about the fusion processor that was the part's main selling point, leaving the register map with no description of it at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: And that's the part that was not explained in the register map at all
claims.speaker: Jeff Roberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: The way in was the vendor's own evaluation kit: its companion board shipped with firmware that configured the processor correctly, so capturing the bus traffic between the two recovered the initialisation sequence.
claims.quote_verbatim: plugs in his, his, uh, logic analyzer and just sniffs the traffic
claims.speaker: Jeff Roberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: The same pattern recurred on a nine-axis part combining gyroscope, magnetometer and accelerometer, where the interface to the motion processor had to be reverse engineered because the register map was withheld.
claims.quote_verbatim: here's our magical chip, but we're not going to show you how to interface to it
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: A gyroscope costs roughly ten times the power of an accelerometer, so leaving it out is worth real battery life if the application can manage without it.
claims.quote_verbatim: gyros take like 10 times the power of an accelerometer
claims.speaker: Brian Faith
claims.episode_title: Open FPGA Toolchains and Machine Learning with Brian Faith of QuickLogic

claims.claim_text: That trade can be tested rather than assumed: removing the gyroscope data from a gesture-classification problem left the accuracy unchanged, which eliminated a dollar part, its power draw and potentially a move from six axes to three.
claims.quote_verbatim: the accuracy of the gesture detection didn't change if we removed the gyro from the equation
claims.speaker: Brian Faith
claims.episode_title: Open FPGA Toolchains and Machine Learning with Brian Faith of QuickLogic

claims.claim_text: Two features decide whether a part is usable in a low-power design: an interrupt output, so a free-fall or motion event wakes the processor instead of being polled for, and lines such as shutdown and reset brought out so the device can be controlled and recovered.
claims.quote_verbatim: you want to like interrupt the micro and say, Hey, take a reading right now
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Rigorous engineering stuff may be out the window

claims.claim_text: Assembling the sensing hardware is the easy part of an inertial measurement project — the parts are catalogue items — and the point of getting the basics working quickly is to free the effort for the algorithms.
claims.quote_verbatim: how fast can we get the basics working so that we can go back to working on algorithms
claims.speaker: Elecia White
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Elecia White - Wirewove Worshipping Wookieist?

claims.claim_text: Firmware should be written against a generic sensor interface rather than the specific part fitted, so that the code has as few dependencies on the rest of the system as possible.
claims.quote_verbatim: I want to talk to a generic accelerometer interface, not the specific STIMU part on the board
claims.speaker: Phillip Johnston
claims.episode_title: Firmware for Hardware Engineers with Phillip Johnston

claims.claim_text: Under Linux the sensor is presented as files: acceleration in each axis appears as a virtual file that is read when a value is wanted, through a subsystem built for this class of device.
claims.quote_verbatim: Linux turns everything into files
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: The driver is what bridges the two: it translates the vendor's register map into that abstraction, so that reading a named file returns the value from a documented register address.
claims.quote_verbatim: that is the driver piece, right, where it's basically abstracting that register set
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: Once the driver probes correctly the hardware work is finished and the sensor is reachable from ordinary application code in any language, which is what the separation between kernel and user space buys.
claims.quote_verbatim: once you're in user space, you're done with hardware
claims.speaker: Jay Carlson
claims.episode_title: Embedded Linux with Jay Carlson

claims.claim_text: Cable movement generates its own charge. Insulation moving against the conductor produces a charge on the cable, and since a typical vibration accelerometer is itself a charge-output device, a test jig whose cabling flexes injects error directly into the measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: It can actually generate a charge in your cable when, when you move it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Wrong Hardware, Wrong Software - Fugacious Fan Funding

claims.claim_text: Calibrated equipment does not rescue a badly built test: a calibrated accelerometer, charge amplifier and shaker will still produce meaningless vibration results if the fixture is wrong, and the check that reveals it is the coherence measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's because you didn't set up your jig properly. You didn't measure your coherence.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Keyzermas All The Way

claims.claim_text: Coherence is not taught as part of a normal course, which is why the failure is common: engineers reach vibration testing without the concept and read the resulting garbage as a fault in the apparatus.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't learn about coherence
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Keyzermas All The Way

claims.claim_text: The physical method for board-level vibration work is to glue a miniature accelerometer directly to the assembly, usually in several places and orientations, and to mount the board in different configurations across successive shakes.
claims.quote_verbatim: You get an accelerometer, a little miniature one. And you would super glue it to your PCB
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: A Noisy Rude Bus

claims.claim_text: The instrument for this work is a dynamic signal analyser rather than a network analyser: designed for audio-band measurement, it takes accelerometer inputs and produces the vibration and seismic spectra.
claims.quote_verbatim: you hook up accelerometers to them and you measure, you know, all sorts of vibrations
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: NASA, WOTW & Modular Design - The NASA Nostalgia

claims.claim_text: Some quantities are settled empirically rather than derived: fitting accelerometers and observing what happens is the engineering answer where calculation would be the scientific one.
claims.quote_verbatim: We have accelerometers on there. Let's throw it out and see what happens.
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: Reunion Impedance Matching and 2023 Predictions

claims.claim_text: Active noise cancellation in a car takes its reference from accelerometers mounted on the suspension, which pick up the vibration that will later become audible after travelling through the chassis into the cabin.
claims.quote_verbatim: we are using accelerometers that are sitting on the car suspension
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: High End Audio with Remco Stoutjesdijk

claims.claim_text: The cancellation itself depends on estimating the acoustic transfer function from the noise source to the listener's position, passing the measured noise through that estimate and inverting it — so the quality of the result follows directly from the quality of the estimate.
claims.quote_verbatim: The, the more accurate your estimation of the transfer function from the noise source to the listener is, the better your cancellation is
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: High End Audio with Remco Stoutjesdijk

claims.claim_text: Head-mounted displays need a fast sensor specifically because of latency: if the image does not follow a quick head movement, the mismatch makes the wearer motion sick.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you turn your head real quick and the screen doesn't move with you, you get super seasick
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Agilent's New Name, Molex's New Owner and PCB artwork - Nonsensical Naming Neolatry

claims.claim_text: A sensor fitted for one purpose often supplies a second: the accelerometer detecting that a laser had been moved also sensed its angle, so tilting the unit downward switched the laser off — a safety interlock with no extra hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: The same accelerometer that detects the laser being moved also has an angle center
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: Free-fall detection is a standard use of the interrupt output: a device thrown into the air woke, connected to the network and returned to sleep before it was caught again.
claims.quote_verbatim: it would wake up, connect to the internet and go back to sleep before you caught it again
claims.speaker: Brandon Harris
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Brandon Harris - Impish Internet Iamatology

claims.claim_text: The same reference design taped to a garage door and wired to a messaging service produced a notification whenever the door stayed open more than five minutes — a real problem solved in a couple of hours with parts already to hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: had it send me a text message. If my garage door was open for more than five minutes
claims.speaker: Brandon Harris
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Brandon Harris - Impish Internet Iamatology

claims.claim_text: The signal carries more identity than expected: machine learning applied to accelerometer data alone can identify which person is wearing the sensor from their walking pattern, without a camera being involved.
claims.quote_verbatim: just using an accelerometer to find or to detect the person who is wearing the sensor
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Generic Nodes with Orkhan Amiraslanov

claims.claim_text: Clinical problems often reduce to adding a few standard sensors to an instrument already in use: assessing how steady a surgeon's hands are meant adding galvanic skin response, an accelerometer and time recording to the existing probe.
claims.quote_verbatim: Add gilbionic skin response, add accelerometer, you know, add time recording
claims.speaker: Shrouk El Attar
claims.episode_title: Creative Engineering with Shrouk El-Attar

claims.claim_text: Orientation can be used as a data source rather than a control input: sampling the three axes once a minute and mapping them to colour produced a continuous record of what position a device — and by extension its owner — had been in through the day.
claims.quote_verbatim: it linearly just maps the XYZ accelerometer values to RGB color values
claims.speaker: Noah Feehan
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Noah Feehan - Biloquistic Blinking Blush

claims.claim_text: A levelling instrument can be built entirely from the sensor and indicators: an outer ring of twelve LEDs for coarse level and an inner ring of four around the sensor for fine, with all sixteen lit once the device is level.
claims.quote_verbatim: outer ring is kind of like a coarse leveling thing. Inner ring is like a fine leveling thing.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Boat Anchor Warehouse

claims.claim_text: A wearable camera used the sensor for a control gesture rather than for measurement: placing the device face down was detected as an orientation and used to switch it off.
claims.quote_verbatim: the way you turn it off is you basically put it face down
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The Nerd Calendar

claims.claim_text: In a security application the sensor's job is to qualify an event rather than to measure motion — confirming the vehicle is stationary before anything is triggered.
claims.quote_verbatim: an accelerometer to make sure that the car is stationary at the time
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Reunion Impedance Matching and 2023 Predictions

claims.claim_text: Balancing machines combine the sensor with the mechanics: a body sitting on rollers above a ball, driven by high-torque motors, balances using the accelerometer for its attitude reference.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's got an accelerometer there, and it just balances on top
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Robots are coming - Ominous Operational Overhaul

claims.claim_text: Not every balancing product contains one: a self-balancing board that appears to sense lean turned out to use a switch, which is a simpler control problem than the two-wheeled vehicle it resembles.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't think it's actually an accelerometer in there
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Dave Young

claims.claim_text: The cost collapse is what changed the design space: measuring ten of them at once became routine, and parts are cheap enough that using several is unremarkable.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's just so cheap and easy to, you know, measure 10 different accelerometers at once
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Robots are coming - Ominous Operational Overhaul

claims.claim_text: The same balancing machine would have needed a ten-thousand-dollar sensor a decade earlier, which is why the applications rather than the technique are what is new.
claims.quote_verbatim: it would have been with a, you know, a $10,000 accelerometer
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Robots are coming - Ominous Operational Overhaul

claims.claim_text: Cheapness produces uses the part was never intended for: a researcher measuring balance for Parkinson's work used off-the-shelf consumer hardware rather than instrumentation.
claims.quote_verbatim: accelerometers are used in a lot of ways that weren't initially intended
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Wearables Might Have Limited Fashion Options - Lachrymogenic Lane Language

claims.claim_text: The origin of the technology was aviation, which is some distance from where the parts are now used.
claims.quote_verbatim: accelerometers used to be used for airplanes
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Wearables Might Have Limited Fashion Options - Lachrymogenic Lane Language

claims.claim_text: Production test can depend on the platform the sensor was designed for: a motion-sensing controller intended to be played with a phone needed a test application running on those devices, which meant supplying them to everyone on the factory line.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had to supply iPod touches to everyone in the factory
claims.speaker: Colin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: As a teaching device the sensor works better shared out than explained: each student takes one sensor from a board, researches what it does and why it would be used, and presents that to the others rather than sitting through an exhaustive account of how it works.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'll have the kids each like pick a sensor and they'll research it
claims.speaker: Charlie Larrabee
claims.episode_title: Technology Instruction with Charlie Larrabee

claims.claim_text: Gesture interfaces built on these sensors are easy to propose and mostly do not survive contact with use: shaking or flicking a device to trigger an action is a neat concept that is rarely practical.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not very practical, I guess
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: HP, IEEE, and Human Interface
